instruction: Use FEniCS from the command line to optimize a porous-flow permeability field. Read /home/user/Desktop/problem_spec.json for the channel domain, design grid, solver mesh, pressure boundaries, impermeable walls, permeability bounds, and high-permeability design budget. Read /home/user/Desktop/baseline_permeability_field.csv as the initial feasible permeability field. You may use /home/user/Desktop/porous_flow_opt_base.py as the starter workflow. Create /home/user/Desktop/permeability_field.csv, /home/user/Desktop/solve_submission.py, and /home/user/Desktop/pressure.xdmf; if the XDMF writer creates a companion .h5 file, keep it in the same directory. The permeability CSV must be 8 by 16, all values must be between 0.1 and 5.0, and the high-permeability design budget allows at most 0.40 of cells to have permeability >= 3.0. Keep the channel domain, pressure boundaries, wall conditions, permeability bounds, and design budget from the problem specification unchanged.
